headline: Park Road Transit and Kennel Demonstration Bookings
reservation: Access beyond Mile 15 of the Park Road is restricted to official transit and tour buses; reservations should be made months in advance. Campground stays and backcountry permits require specific orientations and official check-ins at the Visitor Center; verify current road construction limits via NPS.

days.title: Interior Transit
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from Denali Bus Depot; confirm your ticket’s boarding location.

stops.name: Park Road Transit Bus
stops.detail: Take the official bus into the park interior to scan for grizzly bears, moose, and caribou.

stops.name: Savage River
stops.detail: Walk the loop trail at Mile 15, the furthest point accessible by private vehicle.

days.driving: Allow 4–8 hours for bus transit; road conditions and wildlife sightings dictate the pace.
days.note: Pack all food and water as there are no concessions deep inside the park.

days.title: Tundra and History

stops.name: Denali Sled Dog Kennels
stops.detail: Attend a ranger-led demonstration of the only working sled dog team in a US National Park.

stops.name: Horseshoe Lake Trail
stops.detail: Hike through the boreal forest to a lake frequently visited by local beaver colonies.

days.driving: Allow 40–60 minutes; wildlife crossings frequently slow traffic near the entrance.
days.note: Kennel demonstrations are seasonal; confirm the daily schedule at the visitor center.

days.title: Alpine Perspectives

stops.name: Mount Healy Overlook
stops.detail: Trek upwards for a bird's-eye view of the Nenana River valley and the outer ridges.

stops.name: Murie Science and Learning Center
stops.detail: Explore exhibits on subarctic ecology and the park's ongoing biological research.

days.driving: Allow 20–30 minutes local travel; road closures may affect access to specific trailheads.
days.note: Uphill trails can be strenuous; allow extra time for weather-related pace changes.

intel.title: Visitor Center Hub
intel.text: All transit buses and some narrated tours depart from Denali Bus Depot. Use its parking or a lodging shuttle and follow the check-in time and departure location on your ticket.

intel.title: Extreme Disconnection
intel.text: Cell service ends shortly after the park entrance; satellite communication is recommended for backcountry travelers.

intel.title: Healy Supply Point
intel.text: Healy is the last reliable source for fuel and groceries north of the park; plan your tank accordingly.

intel.title: The 30 Percent Club
intel.text: The mountain is often obscured by clouds; stay multiple days to increase your chances of a sighting.

intel.title: Road Landslides
intel.text: Check official updates for the Pretty Rocks landslide status, which affects access to the park's western reaches.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental in Fairbanks and drive south on the Parks Highway; stock up on bear-safe food storage in town.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are limited to the first 15 miles of the road; RVs should check height clearances for campgrounds.
plan.goldenHour: Stony Hill Overlook at Mile 62 is not reachable by standard park bus in 2026; buses turn around at East Fork near Mile 43. Plan a viewpoint reachable on your booked service and confirm return transport.
